coverage.value: Bible Baptist Mission — biblebaptistmission.org (Pensacola, FL)
coverage.note: PARTIAL HIT. Squarespace site with only four indexed pages: /, /what-we-are, /what-we-believe, /where-we-are. No per-person pages and no per-person giving pages exist — BBM is a funds clearinghouse, and all missionaries live on one roster page, /where-we-are, formatted 'SURNAME, First & First — Country'. Verdict: staff_directory / medium. The roster is longer than the fragments search would surface; a fetch pass on https://www.biblebaptistmission.org/where-we-are would return the whole list in one request and is the single highest-value follow-up from this slice.

coverage.value: Berean Mission — bereanmission.org
coverage.note: DEAD. A domain-restricted search against bereanmission.org returned zero indexed results of any kind, i.e. the domain serves no crawlable content. Name searches surface only unrelated entities: bereanmission.com is Berean Mission Church, a congregation in Millbrae CA; 'Berean Missionary Baptist District Association' (EIN 43-1518143) and 'Berean Mission Alliance' (EIN 20-0691782) in the St. Louis area are associations, not sending agencies with missionary rosters. No evidence Berean Mission Inc. still operates a public web surface.

coverage.value: Fellowship of Independent Missions — resolved to fim.org
coverage.note: IDENTITY RESOLVED, NOT A NEW AGENCY. The brief's guess of fimusa.org is wrong and no such site exists. Per fim.org/about-us/history/, the Fellowship of Independent Missions was formed in 1953 (merger with Sahara Desert Mission) and RENAMED to Fellowship International Mission in 1992; it is headquartered in Allentown PA (not Bensalem), EIN 23-6405291, General Director Dr. Paul Barreca. So 'Fellowship of Independent Missions' and Fellowship International Mission are the same organisation at the same domain — fim.org — which hunt_negatives already records as dead (no /missionaries/ path indexed) and which already carries 9 records in the database. This line item should be closed permanently, not re-probed under a new domain.

coverage.value: Baptist Mid-Missions Canada — no independent domain
coverage.note: NOT A SEPARATE SURFACE. The Canadian arm has no website of its own: bmm.org/contact lists it only as a mailing address (PO Box 308011, Cleveland OH 44130) and the email domain office@bmmcanada.org; bmmcanada.org and bmm.ca return no indexed site. Canadian content is served from the already-mined bmm.org (/serve/where-we-serve/canada, /partner/find-a-missionary, /partner/view-all-missionaries), and Canadian donations route through canadahelps.org/en/charities/baptist-mid-missions/, a platform page not a person page. Baptist Mid-Missions is already worked (206 records) — nothing additional here.

coverage.value: Baptist World Mission regional — baptistworldmission.org + Canadian Board, Moncton NB
coverage.note: NO REGIONAL SURFACE. The only regional entity is the Canadian Board of Baptist World Mission (PO Box 29130 Moncton RPO, North End, NB E1G 4R3), whose stated function per baptistworldmission.org/about-us/contact-us/ is administering monthly payroll to Canada-resident missionaries; it has no website and appears only as a charitydata.ca registration (890107063RR0001). BWM's ~240 missionaries in 49 countries are not published as per-person pages anywhere I could find; the national site remains article-driven, confirming the existing dead verdict. No field or regional sub-sites indexed.

coverage.value: Gospel Fellowship Association regional — gfamissions.org
coverage.note: DEAD VERDICT CONFIRMED, WITH A CORRECTION. The site has been partly redesigned — editorial pages now use clean paths (/mission-vision/, /career/, /serving-our-missionaries/, /leadership-and-staff/) — which could easily be mistaken for a new minable shape. The missionary directory has NOT moved: it is still ASP.NET, at /pages/our-missionaries/ with filters such as /pages/our-missionaries/default.aspx?status=Senior+Missionary and /pages/our-missionaries/default.aspx?type=9&title=...&view=list, and individual profiles at /pages/our-missionaries/details/82/ — an opaque numeric ID with no name, and the detail pages carry the generic <title> 'Gospel Fellowship Association Missions', so neither slug nor title identifies the person. ~270 missionaries in 33 countries sit behind that, unenumerable by search. No separate regional or field GFA sites exist. This is a fetch-pass target (iterate details/N/), not a search target.

needs_review.issue: BBM roster is only partially recovered and no status field was visible
needs_review.finding: Every Bible Baptist Mission record in this file came from search snippets of a single roster page, https://www.biblebaptistmission.org/where-we-are, not from the page itself. The roster is certainly longer than what search surfaced, and the snippets showed only 'SURNAME, First & First — Country' with no active/retired/deceased marker.
needs_review.evidence: Two different country-qualifier queries against the same page returned two disjoint sets of names (Criss/Jones/Fluech/Vournas, then Brigham/Dare/Huggins/Demopoulos), which means the page holds more than search will hand over; a third query with exclusions returned nothing new, so snippet extraction is exhausted.
needs_review.recommendation: Fetch https://www.biblebaptistmission.org/where-we-are once in a fetch pass. It should yield the entire roster in a single request, and should be checked for status markers before any of these people is treated as active — the segment's known memorial-rewrite risk applies to roster lines as much as to profile pages.

needs_review.issue: Two BBM roster lines name one adult where the agency may list a couple
needs_review.finding: 'VOURNAS, Roger — Philippines' and 'Rudiger Hemmer — Germany' were listed with a single first name. Only the named person was emitted.
needs_review.evidence: Roster lines for other families carry both first names explicitly ('CRISS, Robert & Lorna'), so a single name is likely deliberate — but it could also be a truncated snippet.
needs_review.recommendation: Confirm on the fetched roster whether either line carries a spouse. Do not infer one.

needs_review.issue: Two agencies are unenumerable by search but are live fetch targets
needs_review.finding: Gospel Fellowship Association Missions (~270 missionaries) publishes profiles at gfamissions.org/pages/our-missionaries/details/<numeric-id>/ with generic page titles, and Baptist World Mission (~240 missionaries) publishes none at all.
needs_review.evidence: gfamissions.org/pages/our-missionaries/details/82/ appeared in results under the title 'Gospel Fellowship Association Missions' — the ID is opaque and the title identifies nobody, so the numeric-ID rule cannot even be applied.
needs_review.recommendation: Route GFA to a fetch pass that walks details/1..N and reads the person's name out of the page body; that turns a dead search target into a large mineable one. Leave BWM dead.

needs_review.issue: Brief line item 'Fellowship of Independent Missions (fimusa.org)' is based on a false premise
needs_review.finding: There is no fimusa.org. The agency renamed itself Fellowship International Mission in 1992 and is the fim.org entry already recorded dead.
needs_review.evidence: fim.org/about-us/history/ states the 1953 formation as Fellowship of Independent Missions and the 1992 rename; MinistryWatch EIN 23-6405291 lists 'Fellowship International Mission, Inc. / FIM'.
needs_review.recommendation: Merge this name into the existing fim.org negative so no future wave spends budget hunting a domain that never existed.
